identity.name: Every Night, Just Me
identity.subtitle: A postpartum night-coordination system that replaces nightly arguing with a pre-agreed roster, a fairness ledger, and the exact words to make it stick.
identity.one_line_promise: A written, fair night-shift system both adults follow - so she gets a protected sleep opportunity, and nobody has to ask.
identity.journey_position: m01 newborn nights -> couple operating system -> daytime division of labour / reconnection / return to work

customer.target_person: Breastfeeding or formula-feeding mother, 0-12 weeks postpartum, doing 100% of night care while her partner sleeps through or is minimally involved (or, for some buyers, with no partner in the home at all)
customer.situation: She is running every night alone - feeding, settling, soothing - while her partner sleeps, works away, or believes 'helping' means one nappy change. There is no agreed system, so every night is renegotiated by exhaustion and resentment.
customer.trigger: The partner's leave ends / he returns to work - nights silently become 100% hers without a conversation, and every 2am wake-up re-opens whose turn it is.
constraints: Often still breastfeeding, so 'sleep through the night' is not simply available to her
Cultural norms assign night care to the mother by default
Asking directly for help can feel like an accusation
For some buyers there is no partner in the home at all
A deep-sleeper partner may not wake even when the baby cries nearby
customer.emotional_stake: She is not just tired - she keeps score alone. Every uninterrupted hour he gets feels like proof her exhaustion is invisible, and naming it makes her the difficult one. Rage at his calm breathing while she feeds, grief for the relationship, and fear that this is now permanent.

before_state.summary: Doing 100% of nights alone; no agreed system; zero protected sleep blocks; resentment building in silence.

after_state.summary: A written night contract both adults follow; one protected 4-5h block most nights; a named partner shift; a weekly 5-minute review instead of nightly arguments.

mechanism.core: Convert a nightly, exhaustion-driven negotiation into a written, pre-agreed default: a roster both adults follow, a sleep-banker ledger that makes invisible exhaustion visible and tradeable, and ready scripts that pre-negotiate the resistant partner's objections.
mechanisms: A written roster removes the emotional labour of asking (negotiation becomes a pre-agreed default; the schedule asks, not her)
Reframes the partner from 'helper' to 'co-manager' - a status upgrade instead of a request for charity
Schedules milk hand-off (pumped bottle, or partner brings the baby to feed and returns her to the crib) so the mother's protected block is physically real
A sleep banker makes invisible exhaustion visible and tradeable (1 credit = covering a 3-5h night block; 1 payback = a morning sleep-in or 3h afternoon nap; redeemed within 7 days)
Pre-negotiates predictable objections ('I have work tomorrow', 'I don't hear the baby', 'my mother says this is your job') with ready scripts
mechanism.why_it_works: The recurring failure is not unwillingness but the absence of a system: with no written default, the night is renegotiated every time by two people running on no sleep, and the default becomes she owns all of it. Making the division explicit, scheduled and ledged - and giving the partner a named shift rather than a vague request - replaces an endless negotiation with an agreed rule.

path.objective: Map the current broken night reality
Pick the right contract template for her situation
Turn the chosen model into a written schedule
Present it as a system, not a complaint
Operate the contract for a full week
Find what broke and what worked

first_win.action: Fill in 'Tonight's Shift Chart': pick a template (A/B/C), write in two clock times, and text the partner one pre-written line from the script bank.

failure_map.see: TR-PPL-NIGHT-SHIFT-001 failure_point_map (bad night / missed shift / resistance / overwhelm / relapse / escalation)

reentry.protocol: One-page 'we fell off - here's how we get back on' card; no guilt framing.

maintenance.system: Renegotiate the contract every 2 weeks as the baby's sleep pattern changes - this is expected, not a failure.

safety.disclaimer: Educational content - not medical, clinical, or mental-health advice. This system coordinates night-care between adults; it never diagnoses or treats any condition and never replaces professional care.
red_flags: An overwhelming sense of hopelessness, emptiness, or sadness that does not lift even after a good sleep block
Intense anxiety, panic, or rapid heartbeats when thinking about the baby's sleep or night-time
Being unable to fall asleep even when the baby is sleeping and a partner is on duty
Intrusive, frightening thoughts of harm coming to yourself or the baby
Feeling disconnected from your baby, or feeling as though they would be better off without you
escalation_rules: Two or more red flags, consistently, for more than two weeks = seek professional assessment; do not try to manage this with sleep schedules alone
Any acute red flag (thoughts of harm; feeling the baby would be better off without you; physical symptoms such as chest pain, fainting, uncontrolled bleeding, or fever) = act today, not later
Any red flag = stop and route to the verified shared crisis/escalation list (never invent numbers)
This system does not attempt to diagnose or handle these; it stops and routes out
For immediate danger, use the emergency number for the person's country from the verified shared list
